title: Test suite: lua library for lua tests
description:
Many of the lua test files define the same collection of functions for
testing various aspects of lua in wireshark. Remove these duplicated
routines into a separate file (`testlib.lua`) and call them from there.

Several of these test files appear to be copy-pasted from each other,
with some semantic changes introduced to some but not others. Attempted
to centralize on one set of behaviours as much as possible.

The majority of actual tests should be the same, even though I'd like to
change those at some point as well. That said, I tweaked the setup for
some of the tests so that the next person to read them can more easily
understand what number of tests will be run once per pcap, versus once
per frame in the pcap.

There are certainly more improvements that can be made to the lua test
suite, but I'm attempting to minimize gold-plating this first pass.

Found several tests in `test/lua/pinfo.lua` which were commented out
with notes that they should pass but don't. These tests do actually pass
now, so I've uncommented them.

`test/lua/listener.lua` notes that a `Listener`'s `reset()` method never
gets called when run in tshark, and defines such a method just to throw
an error if it does. With my changes it somehow is being called, so I've
commented out the `error()` call with a note.

+----------------------------------------
+-- library name: testlib.lua
+--
+-- Provides common functions for other lua test scripts to use.
+----------------------------------------
+
+local M = {
+    ["groups"] = {},
+}
+
+M.init = function(t)
+    for group, expected in pairs(t) do
+        M.groups[group] = {
+            ["expected"] = expected,
+            ["passed"] = 0,
+            ["failed"] = 0,
+            ["total"] = 0,
+            ["packets"] = 0,
+        }
+    end
+end
+
+-- Indicate a passed test in the named group
+M.pass = function(group)
+    M.groups[group].passed = M.groups[group].passed + 1
+    M.groups[group].total = M.groups[group].total + 1
+end
+
+-- Indicate a failed test in the named group
+M.fail = function(group)
+    M.groups[group].failed = M.groups[group].failed + 1
+    M.groups[group].total = M.groups[group].total + 1
+end
+
+-- Increment the number of packets tracked under the named group
+M.countPacket = function(group)
+    M.groups[group].packets = M.groups[group].packets + 1
+end
+
+-- Get the number of packets tracked under the named group
+M.getPktCount = function(group)
+    return M.groups[group].packets
+end
+
+-- Print a banner reporting test progress
+M.testing = function(group, msg)
+    if msg == nil then
+        msg, group = group, nil
+    end
+    if group then
+        if M.groups[group].packets > 0 then
+            print(string.format("\n-------- Testing %s -- %s for packet # %d --------\n",
+                group, msg, M.groups[group].packets))
+        else
+            print(string.format("\n-------- Testing %s -- %s --------\n",
+                group, msg))
+        end
+    else
+        print(string.format("\n-------- Testing %s --------\n", msg))
+    end
+end
+
+-- Test a condition, report and track its status
+M.test = function(group, name, cond, msg)
+    io.stdout:write(string.format("test %s --> %s-%d-%d...",
+            group, name, M.groups[group].total, M.groups[group].packets))
+    if cond then
+        io.stdout:write("passed\n")
+        M.pass(group)
+        return true
+    else
+        io.stdout:write("failed!\n")
+        M.fail(group)
+        if msg then
+            print(string.format("Got the following error: '%s'", msg))
+        end
+        error(name .. " test failed!")
+    end
+end
+
+-- Print the results of testing
+M.getResults = function()
+    local rv = true
+    print("\n===== Test Results =====")
+    for group, num in pairs(M.groups) do
+        if num.expected > 0 and num.total ~= num.expected then
+            rv = false
+            print("Something didn't run or ran too much... tests failed!")
+            print(string.format("%s: expected %d tests but ran %d tests",
+                    group, num.expected, num.total))
+        end
+        if num.failed > 0 then
+            rv = false
+            print(string.format("%s: passed %d/%d, FAILED %d/%d",
+                    group, num.passed, num.total, num.failed, num.total))
+        else
+            print(string.format("%s: passed %d/%d",
+                    group, num.passed, num.total))
+        end
+    end
+    if rv then
+        -- The python wrapper which performs our lua testing
+        -- expects to see this string in the output if there were no failures
+        print("All tests passed!")
+    end
+    return rv
+end
+
+return M

commits_data.message:
Test suite: lua library for lua tests

Many of the lua test files define the same collection of functions for
testing various aspects of lua in wireshark. Remove these duplicated
routines into a separate file (`testlib.lua`) and call them from there.

Several of these test files appear to be copy-pasted from each other,
with some semantic changes introduced to some but not others. Attempted
to centralize on one set of behaviours as much as possible.

The majority of actual tests should be the same, even though I'd like to
change those at some point as well. That said, I tweaked the setup for
some of the tests so that the next person to read them can more easily
understand what number of tests will be run once per pcap, versus once
per frame in the pcap.

There are certainly more improvements that can be made to the lua test
suite, but I'm attempting to minimize gold-plating this first pass.

Found several tests in `test/lua/pinfo.lua` which were commented out
with notes that they should pass but don't. These tests do actually pass
now, so I've uncommented them.

`test/lua/listener.lua` notes that a `Listener`'s `reset()` method never
gets called when run in tshark, and defines such a method just to throw
an error if it does. With my changes it somehow is being called, so I've
commented out the `error()` call with a note.
